newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ENERGY AFRICA GETS NEW OIL PERMIT IN GABON.
newsitem.headline: ENERGY AFRICA GETS NEW OIL PERMIT IN GABON.

text.p: Energy Africa Ltd affiliate Energy Africa Gabon Ltd has signed a production sharing agreement for the Ofoubou block with the Gabonese government.
Energy Africa announced on Tuesday that the agreement was signed on May 23. It has an indirect interest of 37.5 percent in Energy Africa Gabon.

Ofoubou lies about 40km west of the giant Rabi-Kounga field and the permit extends over an area of 326 square km. A well drilled by Occidental Petroleum Corp in 1992 on Ofoubou intersected a 70 metre oil column but was not tested.

Energy Africa Gabon will act as operator for the joint venture group, which consists of Energy Africa Gabon (60 percent), Gentry International (Gabon) Inc (35 percent) and Thomson and Van Eck International (Gabon) Pty Ltd (five percent).

Energy Africa managing director John Bentley said that the acquisition "builds on the strong position that Energy Africa has established in Gabon and provides a low cost entry to an under-explored area with known oil occurrences."
